baseline_comparison.interpretation: The measured 9843.642 ms runtime-average saving exceeded the 6.3-6.8 second estimate by 3.044-3.544 seconds. Thin-bundle upload and executor-readiness gains were larger than the conservative archive-readback estimate.

lifecycle_fallback_probe.timer_interpretation: The object remained present past 600 seconds from policy application and disappeared only after entering Stopped. This proves auto-delete is not measured from policy application and is consistent with a post-stop interval plus platform reconciliation delay.

latest_rerun_attempt.reason: The streaming cold request completed successfully, but its delete initiation failed and typed inventory remained nonzero. A shell chaining error then admitted three c1 requests before the process was stopped. The run did not proceed to c10 and is not a complete or comparable qualification.

source_and_configuration.difference_scope: Documentation, demo assets, and sample README only; src and deployable sample content are unchanged.

measurement_scope.variance_interpretation: No latency delta is calculated. Four streaming requests plus a cleanup anomaly cannot be compared with either complete nonstream qualification.

incomplete_concurrency_1.reason: The benchmark process was terminated after the failed inventory gate was discovered; no c1 percentile or throughput result is published.

gateway_log_latency_split.interpretation: The aligned ApiManagementGatewayLogs query returned no rows, so backend and gateway-overhead percentiles are not claimed for this incomplete attempt.

cleanup.attribution: Inventory drops followed the 23:50 and 00:00 scoped reaper firings. The sandbox_reaped metric reported two confirmed reaps; typed inventory is authoritative for final zero, and exact deletion attribution for the other two objects is not proven.

latest_nonstream_rerun_attempt.reason: The exact nonstream cold canary completed successfully, but the invocation-handle DELETE again timed out before response headers and inventory remained nonzero. The fail-closed orchestrator stopped before c1; c10 was never started.

delete_failure_diagnosis.classification: ACA invocation-handle delete endpoint response timeout
delete_failure_diagnosis.interpretation: The five failures are content-free timeouts before the ACA service returned response headers; no HTTP rejection or runtime exception occurred after a response. The same deployed code previously returned initial acceptance in 0.944-1.297 seconds. Raising the request bound would change the nonblocking cleanup contract and invalidate the apples-to-apples runtime comparison, so no runtime change was made.

remediations: completed-run deletion is bounded best effort and cannot replace completed output
completed-run deletion budget is 24 s across three seam attempts (8 s first slice) sized from the recorded sandbox_delete range, not the drain window
reaper provisioning and selection use stable app identity plus owner kind
production APIM model resolution honors AZURE_FUNCTIONS_AGENTS_MODEL
tool deadline, transport, protocol, and returned errors increment failure metrics
stream benchmark requires a done event and rejects error or missing terminals

mixed_deployment_rerun_attempt.reason: The c1 stage crossed the overlapping deployment boundary and c10 ran after it. The bcdd-only sandbox_delete_provider_fallbacks metric proved mixed source provenance.
mixed_deployment_rerun_attempt.disposition: Retained as diagnostic history only. No client latency or throughput from this attempt contributes to a benchmark claim.

fix.design: Retain the five-second invocation-handle request_delete initiation. On pre-acceptance timeout or exception, call exact-ID provider.delete_sandbox once under the existing 24-second completed-run budget. Never await the accepted handle LRO and never replace completed output with cleanup failure.
regression_coverage: hung handle is cancelled before exact-ID provider fallback
provider success preserves output and closes resources
provider failure preserves output and lifecycle/reaper backstops
normal accepted path never calls provider
fix.independent_review: No blocking correctness, lifecycle, timeout, cancellation, telemetry, or output-preservation issue found.
fix.comparison_with_bcdd366: Both commits implement the bounded provider fallback and preserve lifecycle/output safety. fd6589e was retained because sandbox_delete_fallbacks unambiguously records pre-acceptance fallback use while sandbox_delete_failures remains the overall failure signal; no cherry-pick occurred.

deployment.deployment_reason: The cleanup implementation changed deployable runtime source.
deployment.released_source_match: hybrid_tools.py and hybrid_observability.py matched fd6589e Git blobs after Windows CRLF was normalized to Git LF

runtime.histogram_percentile_note: p50/p95/p99 are percentile approximations over Application Insights aggregation-bucket averages; sample count, weighted average, minimum, and maximum use valueCount/valueSum/valueMin/valueMax.

gateway_diagnostics.interpretation: No AzureDiagnostics row ingested for the exact window or preceding day. Client-observed dependency spans prove the model and MCP routes but cannot separate APIM backend time from gateway overhead. No value is inferred.

progress_traces.interpretation: Aggregate custom metrics contain all 21 requests; progress trace sampling retained only the listed subset.

comparisons.interpretation: The exceptional cleanup fallback made the run safe and complete, but 17 requests paid the five-second handle bound. Differences beyond that measured cost are treated as natural model and platform variance across measurement days.
